- The buttons along the top of the desktop are now the same as on the phone and the web page: one strip of picture buttons (do, centre, pause, chat, friends, sound, zoom out and in, controls, full screen where there is one, and the menu), with their names where there's room.
- Widgets can be moved all the way to the right and bottom edges at any UI size. In the window and the Wayland wallpaper, the widgets', buttons' and menus' own layers used to stop short of those edges (up to 150 px) at some sizes; they now fill the screen.
- Running along, the villager holds still on screen while the village scrolls under them. They used to shake back and forth by a whole cell each time the view stepped, and by more when zoomed in (a phone zooms in by itself).
- The camera moves along at the villager's pace instead of speeding up and slowing down with each column, and comes to rest square on the cells when they stop.
- Lights no longer flicker as the village scrolls: the glow is worked out again whenever the view moves, not kept a column behind for a frame.
- Aurora Lake no longer shimmers while skating: each row of the ice moves by whole pixels, so the floes and cracks slide by as they are, and the snow's grain and glints stay on the ice. The far shore's spruce and the aurora move by whole pixels too.
- The ski slope, the train window and the drive's hills move by whole pixels as well, so their edges no longer boil.
